newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to continue palm oil imports - BULOG.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to continue palm oil imports - BULOG.

text.p: Indonesia will continue to import crude palm oil to ensure sufficient supply ahead of Christmas, the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan and Eid al-Fitr, Beddu Amang, head of the state logistics agency BULOG, said on Wednesday.
He said the agency would also build up its buffer stock by purchasing 30,000 tonnes of crude palm oil from state-owned plantation, PT Perkebunan Nusantara.

"We will carry out imports the amount and timing of which would be suited to price developments in the local market," Amang said, adding that BULOG has imported 20,000 tonnes of crude palm oil earlier this year in the first phase of the programme.
Amang did not say from where the crude palm oil would be sourced, but traders said they expected the purchases to be made in neighbouring Malaysia, the world's top palm oil producer.
BULOG processes imported oil through local refiners before selling it at a discount to local prices in a bid to drive down prices to levels it considers reasonable.
